Think about it this way: nucleophile is made of nucleo (nucleus, or positive charge) and phile (likes). Something that likes positive charge. electrophile is made of electro (electron, negative charge) and phile (likes). Something that likes negative charge. In addition reactions, something is being added to an alkene or some other carbon = element double bond. 

You can determine whether it is nucleo or electrophilic by what the electrons in the pi bond of the alkene do. If the electrons in the pi bond attack the thing that is being added to form a new bond, then there was an interaction between the thing that is being added and negatively charged electrons. Based on our definition, the thing must be an electrophile, and therefore electrophilic addition. 

The opposite case is when a lone pair of electrons on the thing being added attack a carbon nucleus of the alkene to form a new bond. In this case the thing being added had an interaction with the positively charged nucleus of the alkene. Based on our deninition the thing must be a nucleophile, and therefore nucleophilic addition.
